get_performance_report.description: See how often your ads were shown and clicked, the click-through rate, cost and conversions, by campaign, ad group or keyword, over a date range, with the totals added up for you. Each row is ready to put in a table or a message as it is (beta): name, cost_display (money in the account's currency), clicks, conversions, cost_per_conversion_display and ctr_display, so no step has to divide, format or sort. Rows come back with the one that cost most first. To call rows out, fill in the Flag fields rather than adding a filter step: flagged then holds just those rows, each with the reason in flag, and flagged_count says how many. Every campaign (or ad group or keyword) comes back, including one that showed no ads in the period, with zeros, unless Only rows with activity is on. Dates are days in the account's own time zone, and money is in the account's own currency (returned as currency). The whole report comes back in one go, up to How many rows: there are no pages to loop over.
get_performance_report.name: get_performance_report

parameters.description: The Google Ads account to work in. Pick one, or type its ID, shown at the top of Google Ads (like 123-456-7890), for an account the list doesn't show: it lists only the accounts you can open directly, not those under another manager account.
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: What each row should represent.
parameters.name: level

parameters.description: The period to report on. Ignored when you set both a start and an end date below. Defaults to the last 30 days. Days are the account's own, in its time zone: Last week (Mon–Sun) is the most recent full Monday to Sunday there, and the Last 7, 14 and 30 days end yesterday. The result says which days were covered, in period_display.
parameters.name: date_range

parameters.description: First day to include. Set this with an end date for a custom range.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: Last day to include. Set this with a start date for a custom range.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Only include this campaign. Leave empty for every campaign.
parameters.name: campaign_id

parameters.description: (beta) Leave out campaigns, ad groups or keywords whose ads weren't shown at all in the period, such as paused ones. Off unless you turn it on: they are then listed with zeros.
parameters.name: only_with_activity

parameters.description: (beta) An amount in the account's currency, like 50. A row that cost more than this for each conversion gets the flag "Cost per conversion over $50.00" and is listed in flagged. A row with no conversions has no cost per conversion, so this never flags it: turn on Flag spend with no conversions for those. Leave empty to flag nothing this way.
parameters.name: flag_cost_per_conversion_above

parameters.description: (beta) Flag each row that cost money and got no conversions, as "Spent $312.40 with no conversions", and list it in flagged. A row that cost nothing is never flagged. Off unless you turn it on. With both Flag fields left alone, flagged is empty and flagged_count is 0.
parameters.name: flag_no_conversions

parameters.description: The most rows to get, from 1 to 10,000. Defaults to 100. When there are more, you get the ones that cost most, and the totals add up only those. All of them come back at once.
parameters.name: page_size

parameters.description: Leave empty. The report comes back in one go, so there is no next page to ask for.
parameters.name: page_token

count.description: Number of rows in results. 0 when nothing matched.

currency.description: (beta) The account's currency code, like USD. Every money figure in the report is in it.

flagged.description: (beta) Only the rows whose flag isn't empty, the one that cost most first: those the Flag fields picked out. Always an empty list when neither Flag field is set.

ad_group_name.description: (beta) The ad group the row belongs to. Empty in a report by campaign.

campaign_name.description: (beta) The campaign the row belongs to.

conversions.description: (beta) Conversions, as a number. Google can count part of a conversion, so this may be 1.5.

cost.description: (beta) What was spent, as a number in the account's currency (754.02, not micros).

cost_display.description: (beta) What was spent, written as money in the account's currency, like "$754.02". Show this; no formatting step is needed.

cost_per_conversion.description: (beta) Cost divided by conversions, in the account's currency. Empty when there were no conversions.

cost_per_conversion_display.description: (beta) Cost per conversion written as money, like "$35.91", or "No conversions" when there were none.

ctr_display.description: (beta) Click-through rate as a percentage, like "4.28%".

flag.description: (beta) Why the row is called out, in plain words: "Cost per conversion over $50.00" or "Spent $312.40 with no conversions". Empty when the row is not flagged, and always empty when neither Flag field is set.

impressions.description: (beta) Times the ads were shown, as a number.

name.description: (beta) What the row is about: the campaign's name, the ad group's or the keyword's text, depending on Report on.

flagged_count.description: (beta) How many rows are in flagged. 0 when none are, or when neither Flag field is set.

level.description: The level reported on: campaign, ad_group or keyword.

nextPageToken.description: Always empty: the report comes back in one go.

period_display.description: (beta) The days the report covers, in words, like "Nov 2, 2026 to Nov 8, 2026", for a subject line or heading. Empty for Last business week.

period_end.description: (beta) Last day the report covers, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty for Last business week.

period_start.description: (beta) First day the report covers, YYYY-MM-DD. Empty for Last business week.

results.description: Every row, the one that cost most first. Each has ready-to-show fields (name, cost_display, clicks, conversions, cost_per_conversion_display, ctr_display) beside Google's raw values.

ad_group_name.description: (beta) The ad group the row belongs to. Empty in a report by campaign.

campaign_name.description: (beta) The campaign the row belongs to.

conversions.description: (beta) Conversions, as a number. Google can count part of a conversion, so this may be 1.5.

cost.description: (beta) What was spent, as a number in the account's currency (754.02, not micros).

cost_display.description: (beta) What was spent, written as money in the account's currency, like "$754.02". Show this; no formatting step is needed.

cost_per_conversion.description: (beta) Cost divided by conversions, in the account's currency. Empty when there were no conversions.

cost_per_conversion_display.description: (beta) Cost per conversion written as money, like "$35.91", or "No conversions" when there were none.

ctr_display.description: (beta) Click-through rate as a percentage, like "4.28%".

flag.description: (beta) Why the row is called out, in plain words: "Cost per conversion over $50.00" or "Spent $312.40 with no conversions". Empty when the row is not flagged, and always empty when neither Flag field is set.

impressions.description: (beta) Times the ads were shown, as a number.

name.description: (beta) What the row is about: the campaign's name, the ad group's or the keyword's text, depending on Report on.

time_zone.description: (beta) The account's time zone, like America/New_York. Each day of the report starts and ends at midnight there.

totals.description: The rows in results added up.

cost.description: Cost in account currency, micros divided out.

cost_display.description: (beta) Total cost written as money, like "$1,236.44".

cost_per_conversion.description: (beta) Total cost divided by total conversions. Empty when there were no conversions.

cost_per_conversion_display.description: (beta) The same written as money, or "No conversions".

description: Run your Google Ads: create and pause campaigns, set budgets and keywords, and see how they perform.

google_ads_new_campaign_trigger.description: Runs for each campaign added to a Google Ads account, with its name, status and type. Campaigns already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.bidding_strategy: How it bids, such as MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS.
output.budget_id: The ID of the budget it spends from.
output.channel: Where its ads run: SEARCH, DISPLAY, VIDEO, PERFORMANCE_MAX and so on.
output.end: When it ends, in the account's time zone, if it has an end.
output.name: The campaign's name.
output.start: When it starts, in the account's time zone.

parameters.description: The Google Ads account to watch. Pick one, or type its ID, shown at the top of Google Ads (like 123-456-7890).
parameters.name: customer_id

google_ads_new_lead_form_entry_trigger.description: Runs for each person who fills in a lead form on your Google Ads, with their name, email, phone number and answers. Entries already there when the workflow is turned on don't start it. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.ad_group_id: The ID of the ad group, when there is one.
output.answers: Every standard question answered, by its type in lower case (full_name, email, postal_code, company_name and so on).
output.campaign_id: The ID of the campaign the form ran in.
output.custom_answers: Each question you wrote yourself, with the answer.
output.email: Their email address (or work email), if the form asked.
output.first_name: Their first name, if the form asked for it.
output.full_name: The name the person gave, if the form asked for it.
output.gclid: The Google click ID, for matching the lead to the ad click.
output.last_name: Their last name, if the form asked for it.
output.phone_number: Their phone number (or work phone), if the form asked.
output.submitted_at: When the form was sent, with its time zone.

parameters.description: The Google Ads account to watch. Pick one, or type its ID, shown at the top of Google Ads (like 123-456-7890).
parameters.name: customer_id

parameters.description: Only run for entries from this campaign. Leave empty for every campaign.
parameters.name: campaign_id
